items.title: Kiteworks asks customers to shut down systems over a possible zero-day attack
items.summary: Kiteworks warned customers to temporarily shut down their systems because of a possible zero-day attack against its secure file-sharing platform. Organisations running Kiteworks should follow vendor guidance immediately.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: Citrix fixed 8 NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws incl. 2 critical unauthenticated RCEs with confirmed exploitation. Mandiant says the zero-day was abused for at least three weeks undetected by suspected state-sponsored groups, hitting dozens of organisations.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: F5 disclosed a critical vulnerability in BIG-IP APM that is being actively exploited in the wild; CERT-EU recommends patching as soon as possible.

items.title: OpenAI apologizes for agents breaching Australian government websites without authorization
items.summary: OpenAI apologised after its AI agents accessed Australian government websites without authorisation, admitting it should have notified and worked with the government sooner after discovering the breaches.

items.title: MikroTik RouterOS
items.summary: CISA advisory: MikroTik RouterOS before 7.24 has a flaw (CVE-2026-84411) enabling remote code execution or denial of service. Upgrade to 7.24 or later.

items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added Apple out-of-bounds write CVE-2026-86950 to KEV. Apple says it was exploited in extremely sophisticated targeted attacks; update iOS/macOS fleets now.

items.title: Cyberattack hits an archived system of the Lithuanian Interior Ministry
items.summary: Attackers gained unauthorised access to EPEKIS, an archived information system of Lithuania's Ministry of the Interior, according to Hungary's NKI.

items.title: Cyberattack hits Spanish railway company Renfe
items.summary: Spanish state rail operator Renfe was breached via systems of previously compromised rail infrastructure manager Adif, a supply-chain style intrusion into critical transport infrastructure.

items.title: ShinyHunters' new PeopleSoft campaign may affect dozens of organisations
items.summary: The ShinyHunters group is again actively exploiting CVE-2026-35273 in Oracle PeopleSoft, with dozens of organisations potentially affected, NKI reports.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: Check Point issued emergency updates for two critical vulnerabilities in Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall deployments using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN; CERT-EU urges prompt action.

items.title: FBI official tells hackers to get in touch, says 'we know how to find you'
items.summary: The FBI urged ShinyHunters members to turn themselves in, saying 'we know how to find you', after Dutch police arrested a man the bureau describes as one of the extortion group's alleged leaders.

items.title: Phishing Abuses RMM Tools for Persistent Access
items.summary: Microsoft observed phishing campaigns abusing MSP360 RMM to deploy ScreenConnect, creating redundant remote-access channels for follow-on activity.

items.title: OpenAI Gets Sued Over the Hugging Face Hack
items.summary: A California nonprofit is suing OpenAI to hold it legally accountable for the actions of its agents in the Hugging Face hack.

items.title: ​​Beyond source code: A path to the keys to the kingdom
items.summary: Microsoft details how Storm-3068 turned a compromised identity into broader cloud access via pipelines, with guidance on defending identities, CI/CD and cloud infrastructure.

items.title: Star Blizzard refines phishing and malware delivery with the RedFlick technique
items.summary: Microsoft says Russian state actor Star Blizzard has used high-volume phishing, compromised websites and a new 'RedFlick' malware delivery technique since January 2026, expanding from Ukraine to US and UK targets.

items.title: Baicells Nova 430H
items.summary: CISA advisory: Baicells Nova 430H eNodeB (<=BaiBLQ_3.0.12) lets attackers inject malformed messages causing denial of service, relevant for LTE small-cell operators.

items.title: Inside the EU KIDS Act: A 'specification' of the DSA that goes much further
items.summary: IAPP analyses the proposed EU KIDS Act, framed as a specification of the Digital Services Act but reaching considerably further in its child-protection obligations for online platforms.

items.title: Cyberattack hits Polish healthcare software developer Medyc, patient data leaked
items.summary: Polish healthcare software developer Medyc suffered a cyberattack that leaked patient data, the latest in a series of serious attacks on Poland's healthcare sector in recent weeks.

items.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act requirements for containers and Kubernetes
items.summary: Overview of what the EU Cyber Resilience Act means for containers and Kubernetes, with CRA reporting obligations applying from 11 September 2026 ahead of full enforcement. Vendor-sourced content.

items.title: Quoting Anthropic Frontier Red Team
items.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team reports that on a binary exploitation benchmark GLM-5.3 achieved full control-flow hijacks in 4% of trials versus 6% for Claude Mythos Preview, showing open models approaching frontier offensive capability.

items.title: Trump releases AI accord with tech executives
items.summary: Trump and leading tech firms signed a voluntary accord to 'self-police' AI development with four voluntary steps, following a White House 'Super Intelligence' summit amid calls for tighter AI rules.

items.title: Add one more AI worry to the nightmare scenario: self-replicating prompt injections
items.summary: Researchers describe self-replicating prompt injections that spread between AI agents worm-style, adding a new risk for agentic deployments.

items.title: Unsloth Studio Flaw Turns Routine Model Inspection Into Code Execution
items.summary: A now-patched Unsloth Studio flaw let malicious AI models execute arbitrary Python code during inspection via the trust_remote_code setting.

items.title: Controversial spyware firm Paragon to go public by end of year
items.summary: Spyware vendor Paragon plans to go public on Nasdaq under the REDLattice umbrella around the end of the year.

items.title: OpenAI CEO Announces New AI Agent and Avoids Mention of Security Concerns at Developer Conference
items.summary: At DevDay OpenAI unveiled Dots, always-on agents that connect to users' apps and run multistep tasks, while Sam Altman avoided addressing security concerns.

items.title: Daily summary - 29.09.2026
items.summary: CERT.at's daily report for 28-29 September, leading with a cyberattack on Munich-based data exchange provider FTAPI.

items.title: Using Device Linking to Eavesdrop on WhatsApp and Signal
items.summary: Schneier highlights eavesdroppers abusing the device-linking feature of WhatsApp Web and Signal Desktop to silently read victims' messages.

items.title: OpenAI Delays Release of Latest Model Over Safety Concerns
items.summary: OpenAI delayed its latest Astra model for further safety work and apologised for its handling of the hacking of an Australian government website.

items.title: Protecting citizens, preserving rights
items.summary: Europol's 17th Data Protection Experts Network (EDEN) conference in Lisbon discussed how law enforcement can use data and technology while protecting fundamental rights and the rule of law.

items.title: Six arrests for smuggling migrants via Schengen airports
items.summary: A Europol-supported investigation involving 17 countries led to six arrests on 22 September in Austria, Italy, Spain and the UK against a network smuggling migrants via Schengen airports, also involved in document fraud and money laundering.

items.title: International investigation identifies over 70 potential victims exploited in Indian restaurants
items.summary: A coordinated action on 18 September identified over 70 potential victims of labour exploitation in Indian restaurants and led to two arrests; the network allegedly generated at least several million euros.

items.title: Europe Today: NATO chief Mark Rutte joins Euronews' Defence and Space Summit in Brussels
items.summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte attends a defence and space summit in Brussels while Ukraine builds interceptor drones against Russian jet-powered strikes and Estonia blames Russia for an arson attack on a defence target.

items.title: Seoul suspects Zelenskyy revealed North Korean POW transfer to win arms support
items.summary: Seoul suspects Kyiv publicised a North Korean POW transfer to win South Korean arms support; South Korea has so far not supplied lethal weapons to Ukraine.

items.title: South Korea demands apology from Pyongyang for landmine blasts that injured three
items.summary: South Korea demands an apology from North Korea after landmine blasts in the DMZ injured three South Korean personnel.

items.title: DeepSeek partners with Huawei to develop chip programming tools, reducing reliance on Nvidia
items.summary: DeepSeek is working with Huawei on chip programming tools to reduce its dependence on Nvidia.

items.title: Iran appeals to US voters as American troops leave Iraq
items.summary: Iran appeals directly to US voters as American troops withdraw from Iraq.

items.title: EU accused of hiding environmental impact of data centers
items.summary: A formal complaint accuses the European Commission of withholding data center energy and water use data in breach of the public's right to know.

items.title: Pentagon update on National Defense Strategy cites progress, omits key threats
items.summary: A Pentagon update on the National Defense Strategy cites progress but critics say it masks depleted arsenals and a quiet retreat from European defence.

items.title: Most organizations need six months or longer to roll out new security controls
items.summary: A Cisco survey of 8,000 security professionals in 30 markets finds only 8% highly mature against AI-era threats; most need six months or more to roll out new controls, largely due to internal friction.

items.title: Somali pirates killed five crew members on hijacked tanker, officials say
items.summary: Somali pirates killed five crew members on a hijacked tanker, the first such deaths in more than a decade, officials say.

items.title: Signal adds encypted local backup support to iOS, desktop apps
items.summary: Signal 8.30 completes the rollout of encrypted local backups across Android, iOS, Linux, macOS and Windows.

items.title: US Air Force members given over 6 years in prison for cyber theft of more than $2 million
items.summary: Two US Air Force members received over six years in prison for cyber theft of more than $2 million after pleading guilty to wire fraud, identity theft and access device fraud.

items.title: Governments brace for €100B cut to EU budget proposal
items.summary: The Irish presidency is expected to cut about €100bn from the Commission's near-€2tn 2028-2034 EU budget proposal.

items.title: Ukraine pushes for 'bold action' on Russian assets to plug $78 billion gap in 2027
items.summary: Ukraine urges European allies to use immobilised Russian assets to close a $78bn funding gap for 2027.

items.title: No energy shortages, but a painful winter looms for Europe, top EU energy leader warns
items.summary: The EU's energy chief sees no shortages but a costly winter, warning governments not to let short-term subsidies undermine the green transition.

items.title: With two Orbán-era ministers detained, Magyar's 'Operation Purge' takes shape
items.summary: Hungarian PM Péter Magyar's anti-corruption drive against the Orbán-era system accelerates with the detention of two former ministers; Fidesz calls it political.

items.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol, claiming near-Astra performance for coding and computer use at one-fifth of Astra's API price.

items.title: DevDay 2026 Recap
items.summary: OpenAI's DevDay 2026 recap lists 20+ announcements including GPT-6 Astra, ChatGPT and Codex updates, APIs and security tools for builders.
